core_review: Original publisher paper physical pages2–5 and9–10 manually read; Eq13 visually checked. Selected f_i=1/x_ti is explicitly one of four source predictors, not inferred from a code name. All ten fields are SOURCE_DESCRIPTION_REVIEWED.

h_t=b_t elementwise x_t /(b_t dot x_t), a wealth-drifted holding vector. Eq13 minimizes −f dot b + lambda||b−h||1 +eta/2||b−h||2² +tau/2||b||2² on nonnegative sum1 weights. No covariance estimate, risk-target substitution, or fitting loss is added.

Paper Theorem1 physicalpage5 states existence for nonnegative lambda,eta,tau and uniqueness if eta>0 or tau>0; the selected eta .00025 and tau .00005 yield a strongly convex finite-domain mathematical objective. This does not prove finite solver iterations achieved argmin.

Physicalpages2–3 Eq1–2: after trading net-wealth fraction w solves 1=w+gamma||h−w b_next||1 and next gross price-relative gain multiplies w. This is separate from the lambda=10gamma penalty in allocation selection. Actual gamma, valid commercial fee model, slippage/impact and execution calendar remain unspecified.

Physicalpages9–10 explicitly choose lambda=10gamma,eta .00025,tau .00005 after historical experiments; tables are OLMAR parameter tuning, followed by applying values in all experiments. No OOS or present economic evidence is inferred.

Formal account uses period-close price relatives and next-period target. Initial actual b1 is not fixed in the selected Eq13 definition; inner-solver equal starting vector is not a trading initialization. Assets/data/tradability, missing or zero prices and actual execution mapping remain absent.

Paper physicalpage16 links Ting221/DENRPO; five supplementary code files were statically read (DENRPO1_fun, DENRPO1_run,DENRPO3_fun,w,simplex_projection_selfnorm2). They are not used to upgrade the paper fields. run equal-weight initial portfolio, fzero cost implementation and extreme-vector projection scaling are implementation choices and have not been executed.

Whole DENRPO construction is one family; four predictors, LALM/ADMM solvers, parameter variants and asset universes are not independently counted. Current baseline and six OLPS comparisons show distinct targets/state, not a new implementation of an existing identical rule.

records.definition_signature: RCK:known_IID_joint_finite_return_scenarios_rk_prob_pi; cash_return1; maximize_sum(pi*log(rk.dot(b))); simplex_b; sum(pi*(rk.dot(b))**(-lambda))<=1; lambda=log(beta)/log(alpha); fixed_b_repeated_each_epoch

core_review: Author manuscript physical pages2,3,6,7,8,10,25 manually read including formulas. The selected construction is general finite jointly distributed nonnegative return vectors with a cash component fixed to1, not the two-outcome special case or quadratic approximation.

Fixed b is nonnegative and sums to1. Given joint scenarios and probabilities, alpha,beta in(0,1), lambda=log(beta)/log(alpha)>0, Eq7/11 maximize sum pi log(r dot b) subject to sum pi(r dot b)^(-lambda)<=1. Log-sum-exp form uses only positive-probability support. Positive support payoffs must be positive; all cash feasible does not impose a strictly positive cash holding.

IID return vectors across rounds and a constant rebalanced wealth fraction b are model assumptions. w1=1 and w_t is the product of earlier portfolio return multiples; fixed proportions are not fixed shares or an online probability-refitting procedure.

Physicalpage7 Eq6 states the sufficient implication to Prob(inf w_t<alpha)<beta. Its risk is below initial wealth, not peak-to-trough maximum drawdown; no sell-at-alpha stop is invented. The bound is conditional and conservative, not empirical financial assurance.

Physicalpage8 all risky expected returns<=1 permits an all-cash optimum, not a separately triggered exit rule. lambda approaching0 is the ordinary Kelly limit; illustrative alpha .7,beta .1 are not frozen account defaults. General RCK is not simply a fractional-Kelly scalar rescaling.

Only nine fields are SOURCE_DESCRIPTION_REVIEWED. cost remains MISSING: r_cash=1 is a mathematical convention, not evidence that commissions, spread, impact, interest and taxes vanish. Numerical solver/uniqueness/ties and data/clock/execution contracts are not supplied or executed.

The author HTML explicitly names Busseti,Ryu,Boyd and links the exact manuscript URL plus cvxgrp/kelly_code. This authenticates source identity but no code was reviewed or run and code permission would not license paper/data.

Whole-family adjudication compares joint risk feasible set, objective and fixed state, not an API/title/solver name. Its full negative-power moment risk constraint distinguishes it from ordinary Kelly sizing, mean-variance, CORN historical wealth maximization and UP wealth averaging. One selected family is eligible; alpha/beta values, solvers and output forms are not separate additions.

dedup.reason: 和普通Kelly使用单一概率不同，本构造同时对若干可能联合概率求最坏期望增长；与RCK已知概率下负幂矩可行域不同。已回M1162精确原站，其核心为Wasserstein集合下收益减低收益短缺惩罚，且有指数暴露约束，不是log效用的有限概率凸包构造。ONS/UP/CORN/DENRPO均无此目标。仍属于组合增长优化的相关研究族，不宣称经济独立；新增计数待独审。 有限联合收益情景上，对多个可能概率向量的凸包取最坏预期log增长，再选择固定长多财富配置。此完整目标不同于给定分布下的RCK概率风险约束、M1162低收益短缺惩罚DRO、CORN样本财富目标或DENRPO正则调仓。不是换论文标题/库/参数/求解器；DRKP整族只计1，其他不确定集不拆数，不主张经济独立。

source_comparisons.finding: Original exact Sina page section3.1 objective image maximizes worst expected linear portfolio return minus phi times positive-part shortfall from a reference return. It explicitly describes a Wasserstein distribution ball. The dual image retains index/factor exposure and weight constraints. Neither objective is log utility, and this is not the selected DRKP finite probability-vector convex hull. This distinguishes definitions without inventing missing phi or claiming historical backtest reproduction.
source_comparisons.rights: Source and image permission not inferred; all raw objects ignored; comparison evidence only.

core_review: Original author PDF physicalpages1–4 manually read and formula images inspected. The selection is section2.1 finite convex hull of probability vectors and basic long-only simplex; the paper allows general B, but no unprinted constraints are added.

For fixed nonnegative joint return matrix R with cash row1 and probability vectors pi_j, maximize over b>=0,sum b=1 the minimum_j sum_k pi_jk log(r_k dot b). Linearity in pi makes this equal inf over their convex hull, not an average probability or worst single outcome. The allocation b is the only selected optimization variable.

Return vectors are IID across rounds and a fixed wealth fraction b repeats. Current wealth times b is allocated before the next return realization. No rolling probability training or hindsight choice of b is invented. All-cash returns1 and log0 in every scenario, but this is not real-world loss protection.

Only support occurring with positive probability under at least one candidate distribution requires strictly positive portfolio payoff for a finite log objective; all-zero support columns contribute nothing. No uniqueness, solver tolerance or finite numerical convergence claim is added.

The worst case is expected log growth across a specified distribution set; it is not CVaR, a max-min one-round return, or a peak/initial-wealth drawdown bound. Unlike RCK there is no negative-power moment risk constraint. With a singleton probability set it reduces to ordinary Kelly, a boundary not a separate addition.

9 fields retain SOURCE_DESCRIPTION_REVIEWED; cost remains MISSING. Cash return1 is a mathematical convention, not a zero fee/interest assertion. No real asset universe, probability estimator, input window, order mapping or numerical implementation is frozen.

The author page links the exact manuscript and repository. Its subtitle abbreviates the first author as S.Sun, whereas original manuscript page1 states Qingyun Sun; attribution follows the manuscript, the observed HTML abbreviation difference is retained and not silently normalized into independent evidence.

The appendix/example pertains to a box probability set and is outside the selected finite-hull definition. No formula from that implementation/example is used to fill the finite-hull solver or validate performance. No upstream code or optimization was executed.

Whole-family dedup uses actual targets/state/uncertainty. M1162 exact source uses linear gain minus reference-shortfall penalty under a Wasserstein ball; RCK constrains a known distribution; CORN maximizes wealth of selected history; six OLPS algorithms and DENRPO do not optimize this whole function. Different ambiguity-set variants, radii, solvers or sample counts are not split into new records.
